title: bug: check-architecture run from the candidate's own packages/moe-daemon/dist trusts every module index.ts imports, but requiredChecks scripts protect only the files they name
description:
In Moe's own repo, the CQ-V10 check `node packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js check-architecture --rules arch.json` runs code built from the candidate. V01 protected drift covers only the listed scripts (checkArchitecture.ts, architectureRules.ts). A candidate can still change the verdict with no protected-check-changed token by editing context/repositorySource.ts, util/cachedPlanPaths.ts, util/logger.ts, or any other module dist/index.js loads, for example by serving '' content or by overriding stdout/exitCode.
Fix (at activation, V12): run the check from a runner-provisioned trusted install built at the base revision, or protect the import closure. This is not exploitable today, because nothing dispatches the check and verified-local is off.
definitionOfDone: A candidate that edits a non-listed module the checker imports cannot turn a failing architecture check into a delivered pass.
Legacy/observe behavior unchanged; tests pin the refusal.

implementationPlan.description:
packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/requiredChecks.ts: the installed-checker classifier. It is pure: no I/O and no state.

- `export const INSTALLED_ARCHITECTURE_CHECK = /^moe-daemon check-architecture(?: [A-Za-z0-9._\/=:@+^~-]+)*$/;`
  - Single spaces between words.
  - No quote, operator, variable, redirection or newline can appear, so nothing else can run before or after it, or change it.
- `export function untrustedArchitectureChecks(defs: readonly ProtectedCheckDefinition[]): string[]` returns, in definition order, the ids of the defs that are architecture checks but whose trimmed command fails INSTALLED_ARCHITECTURE_CHECK.
  - A def is an architecture check when its command matches /check-architecture/i, or when its scripts include a path ending 'src/commands/checkArchitecture.ts' or 'src/delivery/architectureRules.ts'.
  - The second signal catches an npm-script wrapper whose approver listed the checker's sources.
- The doc comment states why. `node packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js check-architecture` is code the candidate builds: index.ts loads every module the daemon imports, and requiredChecks protects only the files it names. So any of those modules (repositorySource, cachedPlanPaths, logger, ...) could serve '' content or override stdout and exitCode. The installed form is the checker that the runner provisions from a trusted install built at the base revision (activation, CQ-V12).

Error handling: defs come from an approved snapshot that is already validated. Read command and scripts defensively anyway (typeof checks), so that a malformed def counts as an architecture check that is not in the installed form (refused) and never throws.
implementationPlan.note: Round 2: the classifier logic is unchanged and reused. The landed untrustedArchitectureChecks already encodes the rule: the mention signal, the source signal, and the installed-form regex. policy.ts now passes the owed gate through it as a pseudo-definition {id:'(qualityGate)', command} that protects no files, so the gate and definitions share one rule. The only edit in requiredChecks.ts is one doc-comment sentence (+2/-1) recording that dependency. No new export, no behaviour change.

implementationPlan.description:
packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/policy.ts: refuse a candidate-built architecture checker under verified-local only. EDIT the bytes 43088e9b and V06 landed.

- `export const UNTRUSTED_CHECKER_PREFIX = 'required-check-untrusted-checker:'`, together with a token helper beside protectedCheckChangedToken.
- In protectedCheckShortfall, when `trusted !== null` (the verified-local branch) and defs is a non-empty approved list, put one token per id from untrustedArchitectureChecks(defs) first in the result, then the existing drift and owed tokens.
  - Every other branch is unchanged.
  - Legacy still returns before this point in evaluateDeliveryEvidence, and observe (trusted === null) never sees the token.
- describeMissingEvidence: a token with that prefix reads "required check <id> runs the architecture checker from code the candidate builds; under verified-local its command must be exactly the installed `moe-daemon check-architecture ...`, which the runner provisions from the base revision". The id comes from the approved snapshot, never from candidate data.
- A short comment cites task-efbf1742. Every consumer of evaluateDeliveryEvidence (qa_approve, dependency satisfaction, the delivery projection) already reads a missing token as not satisfied, so no other edit is needed.

No submit_plan change. A plan-time refusal would mean editing the shared submitPlan.ts; the delivery refusal is the gate that matters, and V12's integration can add the plan-time message.

Error handling: the classifier never throws. If it did, the existing try/catch in protectedCheckShortfall already reports protected-checks-unmeasured, which fails closed.
implementationPlan.note:
Round 2 fix for QA issue 2 (gate-only bypass), in delivery/policy.ts:
- Adds private `QUALITY_GATE_CHECK_ID = '(qualityGate)'`. No definition id can take it, since ids match /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/.
- checkShortfall, under verified-local only (`trusted` non-null; an empty env list counts as strict, like protectedCheckShortfall), judges the owed gate through untrustedArchitectureChecks([{id, command}]):
  - "Owed gate" is owedGate: the live qualityGate, or requiredCheckAtDone once DONE.
  - An untrusted form gives `required-check-untrusted-checker:(qualityGate)`. It comes FIRST, then `required-check:<gate>` if no pass, so a passing run never clears it.
  - A null gate still returns [] before any lookup.
- describeMissingEvidence names "the quality gate (settings.qualityGate)" for that id.
- The header doc is updated.
No projection change is needed: the token shares UNTRUSTED_CHECKER_PREFIX, which requiredCheckSatisfiedFor already enumerates. Legacy keeps its early return, and observe has trusted === null.

comments.author: worker-093a65d0
comments.content:
Response to qa_reject #1 (worker-093a65d0).

Issue 2, the qualityGate route (policy.ts:446): accepted. A gate command that names the checker is a recognizable form, and it slips past the classifier.
Fix: under verified-local, checkShortfall judges the gate the task owes, through the same untrustedArchitectureChecks, as a definition that protects no files. "The gate it owes" means the live qualityGate, or requiredCheckAtDone once the task is DONE.
- An untrusted form gets `required-check-untrusted-checker:(qualityGate)`. No definition id can take that label: ids start alphanumeric and contain no parentheses.
- The token is listed before `required-check:<gate>`, and a passing run never clears it.
- Rows: a gate-only task, a gate alongside passing definitions, the installed gate (delivers), and the DONE requiredCheckAtDone route. Each row checks the projection and dependents too. Legacy and observe stay unchanged.

Issue 1, the opaque wrapper `bash scripts/lint.sh`: this row leaves it as is. Architect-4ae016fb ruled on it in this channel (chat msg-b2345781, 08:32:51) and added an addendum on V12 (task-b621ddc9 comment-bde17873, 08:33:02). It is a pre-activation V12 requirement and does not block DoD 1 here.
Technical reason: the def's command and protected paths name neither the checker nor its sources. Only lint.sh's bytes do, and the classifier reads only approved definition text. evaluateDeliveryEvidence is synchronous and reads no blobs. The same def could run an unprotected helper.sh with no checker at all. That is the general V01 limit: protection covers only what the approver names.
The binding fix is V12's trusted check guest, in which moe-daemon resolves only to the base-revision install. An approval-time scan of the protected wrapper bytes would be optional defense in depth.

comments.author: architect-4ae016fb
comments.content:
Architect scope ruling for DoD 1 (architect-4ae016fb, efbf1742's planner, 2026-10-30). This is a durable copy of chat msg-b2345781 (08:32:51Z). qa-ba3f4f35 acknowledged it in msg-9da6fb19.

In scope, and blocking if missed: DoD 1 covers every required check the daemon can recognize as an architecture check. That means:
- its approved command mentions the checker (/check-?architecture/i), or
- its protected scripts include commands/checkArchitecture.ts or delivery/architectureRules.ts.
Under verified-local, each such check must be exactly the installed `moe-daemon check-architecture [args]`, or the gate refuses it with `required-check-untrusted-checker:<id>`. The same holds for the owed qualityGate route (QA comment-6897055b; the worker accepted it in comment-708a213d). A recognizable form that slips past the classifier still blocks this row.

Out of scope here: the opaque protected wrapper from QA comment-c6b761b4.
- Example: `{id:'arch', command:'bash scripts/lint.sh', scripts:['scripts/lint.sh']}`, where lint.sh's bytes run the candidate-built dist checker.
- Neither its command nor its protected paths name the checker, and the classifier is pure: it never reads blob content.
- This is the general V01 limit, where a protected entry executes unprotected candidate code. The same def could run an unprotected helper and exit 0 with no checker at all.
- V12 (task-b621ddc9, comment-bde17873) owns it as a pre-activation requirement: a trusted check guest in which `moe-daemon` resolves only to the base-revision install, plus an optional approval-time scan of the protected wrapper bytes.

QA's approval should record this residual and its owner. It is not reachable today: verified-local is off and nothing dispatches checks.
